mainTopic: Whether blood is called פר, and whether the כהן גדול's יום הכפורים bull is a private or communal offering
overview: This amud first finishes the argument between רבי יצחק נפחא and רבי אמי over whether a slaughtered bull is still called a פר. רב פפא narrows the dispute: everyone agrees the body is called פר, and they argue only about the blood. רב אשי supports the view that blood is called פר from 'בפר בן בקר', and the other side reads that פסוק differently. The גמרא then asks why the bull of a כהן גדול who died is not simply left to die, like any חטאת whose owner died. רב עמרם answers that it is a חטאת צבור. The גמרא tries to support this from a משנה with רבי מאיר and רבי יעקב, but shows that their words prove nothing. It explains that the real rule for pushing aside שבת and טומאה is a fixed time. אביי then brings ברייתות that call the bull communal. רבא answers that it is really a 'partners' offering, and explains the practical difference: כהנים do not bring a פר for a mistaken ruling. The amud ends by introducing a new proof from a question of רבי אלעזר, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A verse calls the slaughtered bull a bull
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא challenges רבי אמי using the פסוק 'and he shall take out the whole bull'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא challenged רבי אמי: The verse says 'And he shall take out the whole bull'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק נפחא attacks רבי אמי's view with a פסוק. This פסוק calls the animal a 'bull' even after it was slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי holds that once the bull is slaughtered, it is no longer called a פר. But this פסוק is about the remains after the שחיטה, when the fats have already been offered. It still says 'the whole bull', which seems to show the name stays.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (usually from a source)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha challenged
phrases.notes: An objection based on a source

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami:
'And he shall take out the whole bull'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא ד:יב, said after the slaughter

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier dispute about whether a slaughtered bull is still called פר
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's view that a slaughtered bull is no longer called פר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah uses the word 'bull' for the carcass after slaughter, so the name must still apply

steps.title: The verse means taking out all of it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that the word 'whole' means removing everything that is left, not that it is still called a bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means that he should take out all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי defends his view. He reads the פסוק as a command to take out all of the remains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the פסוק is the word 'כל', which tells us to take out everything. The word פר just tells us which animal the remains came from. It does not prove that the carcass is still technically called a פר.

phrases.english: That he should take out all of it.
phrases.notes: The focus is on 'whole', not on the name 'bull'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק calls the carcass a 'bull'
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only demands that all the remains be removed

steps.title: A second verse about the sin-offering bull
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another פסוק that calls the animal a bull after its blood was brought inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the bull of the sin-offering and the goat of the sin-offering' (whose blood was brought in, shall be taken outside).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק that raises the same problem against רבי אמי. This sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק about יום הכפורים speaks of the animals after their blood was already brought into the קודש הקדשים. It still calls them 'bull' and 'goat'. The answer from step 2 does not work here, because the word 'כל' does not appear.

phrases.english: 'And the bull of the sin-offering
and the goat of the sin-offering',

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵת פַּר הַחַטָּאת וְאֵת שְׂעִיר הַחַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge of the same kind, after step 2 answered the first one
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After the blood was brought inside, the animal is still called 'bull'

steps.title: רב פפא narrows the dispute to the blood
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says everyone agrees that the body with its hide, flesh and dung is called a bull. The only disagreement is whether the blood alone is called a bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Regarding the hide, flesh and dung, everyone agrees. Where they disagree is about the blood. One master holds that blood is called 'bull', and the other master holds that blood is not called 'bull'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by redefining what the argument is about. The carcass is called a bull according to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because both sides agree that the body is a פר, פסוקים about burning the carcass outside cannot prove anything. The real question is whether the blood by itself, which is brought inside, carries the name פר.

keyTerms.meaning: Dung, the contents of the intestines

steps.whyThisMatters: It changes the whole dispute. The question is no longer 'slaughtered or not' but 'body or blood'.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Regarding the hide, flesh and dung,
everyone agrees (they are called 'bull').
phrases.notes: So the verses in steps 1 and 3 are no challenge

phrases.english: Where they disagree is about the blood.
One master holds: blood is called 'bull',

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: דָּם לָא אִיקְּרִי פַּר.
phrases.english: and the other master holds: blood is not called 'bull'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא בְּעוֹר וּבָשָׂר וָפֶרֶשׁ דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by redefining the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute is about the slaughtered carcass
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees about the body. The dispute is only about the blood.

steps.title: רב אשי proves that blood is called a bull
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says it is more logical that blood is called פר, because the כהן גדול enters 'with a bull', which can only mean with its blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is logical to follow the one who says blood is called 'bull'. As it is written: 'With this אהרן shall come into the Holy, with a young bull.' Does he bring it in by its horns?! Rather, he brings in its blood, and the verse calls that 'bull'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes a side in the dispute that רב פפא defined. He brings a פסוק as support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול obviously does not bring a live bull into the קודש הקדשים. All he brings in is its blood. Since the פסוק still says 'with a bull', it seems that blood is called פר.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...?! (a rhetorical question)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is logical to follow the one who says
blood is called 'bull',
as it is written: 'With this Aaron shall come into the Holy,
with a young bull',
Does he bring it in by its horns?!
phrases.notes: Meaning: obviously he does not bring in the whole animal

phrases.english: Rather, with its blood,
and it calls it 'bull'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי מִסְתַּבְּרָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר דָּם אִיקְּרִי פַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports one side of the dispute that רב פפא defined
steps.raayaObject: The view that blood is called פר
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא טז:ג, 'בזאת יבא אהרן אל הקדש בפר בן בקר'

steps.title: How does the other view read this verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the opposing view explains the פסוק of 'with a bull'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the one who says blood is not called פר deals with רב אשי's פסוק. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for the other side's reading, not an attack. רב אשי only said his view is 'more logical', so the other side can still read the פסוק differently.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (how does he explain it)?

phrases.english: And the other one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opposing view handles step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the view that blood is not called פר explains 'בפר בן בקר'

steps.title: The bull qualifies Aaron to enter
steps.stepSummary: The other view reads the פסוק as telling us what makes אהרן fit to enter: the bull brought as a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what was אהרן made fit to enter the Holy? With a young bull for a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side's reading. The פסוק is not describing what he carries in, but what allows him to enter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, 'בזאת' means 'through this he is qualified'. The bull that was offered as a חטאת is what gives אהרן permission to enter. So the פסוק never calls the blood a פר, and רב אשי's proof is pushed aside.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that the body of a slaughtered bull is called פר. The dispute is only about the blood. רב אשי proves from 'בפר בן בקר' that blood is called פר, but the other view reads that פסוק as describing what qualifies אהרן to enter.

phrases.english: With what was Aaron made fit
to enter the Holy?
With a young bull for a sin-offering.
phrases.notes: The bull qualifies him to enter. It is not what he carries in.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמָּה הוּכְשַׁר אַהֲרֹן לָבֹא אֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק describes what qualifies אהרן to enter, not what he carries in

steps.title: Why not apply the rule of a sin-offering whose owner died?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the whole question. The first כהן גדול died, and a חטאת whose owner died is left to die, so the bull should be unusable anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him figure it out from the fact that this bull is a חטאת whose owner died. A חטאת whose owner died is left to die!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the earlier question was even needed. There is a known rule that should settle it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a fixed rule that a חטאת whose owner died cannot be offered. It is left to die. If the first כהן גדול died, his bull is such a חטאת, so the replacement obviously cannot use its blood, and the earlier question should never have come up.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it from (a different, simpler source)
It goes to death. It is locked away until it dies.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'its owner died' with the animal dying. The owner is the person who brought the offering. Because that person died, the animal itself is left to die.

phrases.english: And let him derive it
phrases.notes: A classic challenge formula: 'why not get the answer from here?'

phrases.english: from the fact that it is a sin-offering whose owners have died
and a sin-offering whose owners have died is left to die!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּחַטָּאת שֶׁמֵּתוּ בְּעָלֶיהָ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the earlier question about the replacement כהן גדול and challenges whether it was needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The question of whether the replacement כהן גדול may use the first כהן גדול's bull
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known rule (חטאת שמתו בעליה למיתה אזלא) already settles the case, so the question is unnecessary.

steps.title: The כהן גדול's bull counts as a communal sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם answers that the כהן גדול's bull is a חטאת צבור. The rule of a חטאת whose owner died only applies to a private offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר רב אדא said to רבא: Your students say that רב עמרם said: it is a communal sin-offering, and it is not left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered. The bull is treated as a communal offering, so the 'left to die' rule does not apply to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of חטאת שמתו בעליה applies only to a private (יחיד) offering. Communal offerings are never left to die. The כהן גדול's bull atones for him and for all his fellow כהנים, so רב עמרם counts it as a חטאת צבור. That is why the earlier question is still a real question.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא whose teaching is being reported

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the passage. The גמרא will now look for a תנא who agrees that this bull is communal.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא לְרָבָא
phrases.english: Ravin bar Rav Adda said to Rava
Your students say
that Rav Amram said
It is a communal sin-offering
phrases.notes: Because it atones for all the כהנים, not just the כהן גדול

phrases.english: and it is not left to die.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי תַּלְמִידָיךָ, אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם: חַטַּאת צִבּוּר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the offering into a different category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bull is the כהן גדול's private offering, so it is left to die when he dies.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bull counts as a חטאת צבור, and communal offerings are never left to die.

steps.title: An attempted proof from רבי מאיר's words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה where רבי מאיר stresses that the יום הכפורים bull is a private offering. It suggests this means some other תנא holds that it is communal.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי מאיר said to him: But the יום הכפורים bull, the כהן גדול's חביתין, and the פסח are private offerings, and they push aside שבת and טומאה. Doesn't that imply that someone holds they are communal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to find a תנא who supports רב עמרם's idea that the bull is communal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר goes out of his way to call these offerings 'private' (יחיד). The גמרא reads this as if he were arguing with someone who calls them 'communal' (צבור). If so, that other opinion would back up רב עמרם.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The daily flour offering brought by the כהן גדול
Pushes aside שבת and ritual impurity. It may be offered even then.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna
Rabbi Meir said to him
But what about the Yom Kippur bull
and the High Priest's wafer-offering, and the Paschal offering
which are individual offerings
and they override Shabbat and ritual impurity.

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִכְּלָל דְּאִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּצִבּוּר?
phrases.english: Does this not imply that there is someone who says they are communal?
phrases.notes: This is the point of the proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו מִכְּלָל דְּאִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּצִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for a תנא who supports רב עמרם's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That the יום הכפורים bull can be counted as a communal offering
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's words in the משנה, which seem to argue with someone who calls these offerings communal

steps.title: The same logic would lead to an absurd result
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי יעקב calls certain offerings 'communal', and by the same logic someone would have to call them private, which no one does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning: it teaches that רבי יעקב said to him: But the bull for a communal mistake, the goats for עבודה זרה, and the חגיגה are communal offerings, and they push aside neither שבת nor טומאה! Does that imply that someone holds they are private?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. If we read רבי מאיר that way, we would have to read רבי יעקב the same way, and that makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב labels some offerings as 'communal' (צבור). Using the same logic, we would conclude that someone calls them 'private', but no one says that. So a label in an argument does not show that someone holds the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull brought when the community sins by mistake because of a wrong ruling of the court
The goats brought for a communal sin of idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying these offerings really are private. It is saying the method of proof is broken, because it would force us into a conclusion nobody holds.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, regarding what it teaches
Rabbi Ya'akov said to him

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר
phrases.english: But what about the bull for an unwitting communal sin
and the goats for idolatry, and the Festival peace-offering
which are communal offerings

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דּוֹחִין לֹא אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא אֶת הַטּוּמְאָה!
phrases.english: and they override neither Shabbat nor ritual impurity!
Does this imply that there is someone who says they are individual offerings?!
phrases.notes: Said with surprise. Obviously no one holds this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 10 by applying the same logic to a parallel statement.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference drawn from רבי מאיר's wording
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same reasoning, applied to רבי יעקב, leads to a conclusion nobody holds.

steps.title: רבי מאיר was arguing against a general rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what רבי מאיר really meant. He was answering the תנא קמא's broad rule that private offerings never push aside שבת and טומאה. He was not answering someone who calls these offerings communal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he was responding to the תנא קמא, whom he heard say: communal offerings push aside שבת and טומאה, and private offerings push aside neither שבת nor טומאה. רבי מאיר said to him: Is 'private offering' a fixed rule? But the יום הכפורים bull, the כהן גדול's חביתין, and the פסח are private offerings, and they do push aside שבת and טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true reading of רבי מאיר. He called these offerings 'private' only to show that the תנא קמא's rule has exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא made a sweeping rule: private offerings never push aside שבת or טומאה. רבי מאיר answered with private offerings that do push them aside. They are still private offerings; they are simply exceptions to the rule. So his wording does not show that anyone calls the יום הכפורים bull communal, and the proof for רב עמרם falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (unnamed) opinion in a משנה
A general rule with no exceptions

steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to support רב עמרם from the משנה fails. רבי מאיר called the יום הכפורים bull 'private' only to break the תנא קמא's general rule, not to argue with someone who calls it communal.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: לְתַנָּא קַמָּא קָא מַהְדַּר לֵיהּ
phrases.english: Rather, he was responding to the first tanna
because he heard him say

phrases.aramaic: קׇרְבַּן צִבּוּר דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְאֶת הַטּוּמְאָה
phrases.english: Communal offerings override Shabbat and ritual impurity
and individual offerings do not override

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא אֶת הַטּוּמְאָה.
phrases.english: neither Shabbat nor ritual impurity.
Rabbi Meir said to him
Is 'individual offering' a fixed rule?
phrases.notes: In other words: your rule has exceptions.

phrases.english: But what about the Yom Kippur bull
and the High Priest's wafer-offering, and the Paschal offering
which are individual offerings
and they override Shabbat and ritual impurity!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לְתַנָּא קַמָּא קָא מַהְדַּר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the rejection by giving the correct reading of רבי מאיר's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading whom the statement in the משנה was aimed at
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר was arguing with someone who calls the bull communal.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר was showing exceptions to the תנא קמא's general rule about private offerings, so his words give no support to רב עמרם.

steps.title: רבי יעקב: being communal is not the deciding rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב challenges the תנא קמא's idea that every קרבן צבור pushes aside שבת and טומאה. He lists communal offerings that do not push them aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יעקב said to him: Is 'communal offering' really a rule? There are the bull for a communal mistake (פר העלם דבר של צבור), the goats for עבודה זרה, and the חגיגה. They are communal offerings, yet they push aside neither שבת nor טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still explaining the quoted משנה. Here it shows that רבי יעקב, like רבי מאיר, was reacting to the תנא קמא's general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said communal offerings push aside שבת and טומאה. רבי יעקב gives three communal offerings that do not, so 'communal' cannot be the real reason. His point is about which offerings push aside שבת, not about labeling any offering as communal or private.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull brought when the community sins by mistake because of a wrong ruling of the בית דין
Goats brought for a communal mistake involving idolatry

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yaakov said to him:
phrases.notes: He is answering the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: Is 'communal offering' a general rule?

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר,
phrases.english: But there is the bull for a communal mistaken ruling,
and the goats for idolatry, and the festival offering,
which are communal offerings,
and they do not push aside Shabbat
nor ritual impurity!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב: קׇרְבַּן צִבּוּר כְּלָלָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 12 showed that רבי מאיר was answering the תנא קמא. This step shows that רבי יעקב was too, so his words also prove nothing about the bull's classification.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's rule that every קרבן צבור pushes aside שבת and טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some offerings are communal yet do not push aside שבת or טומאה, so being communal cannot be the deciding factor.

steps.title: The real rule: a fixed time decides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the correct rule. An offering with a fixed time pushes aside שבת and טומאה, even if it is private. An offering without a fixed time does not, even if it is communal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, hold on to this rule: Any offering with a fixed time pushes aside שבת and טומאה, even if it belongs to one person. Any offering without a fixed time pushes aside neither שבת nor טומאה, even if it belongs to the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the 'communal vs. private' rule with the true principle: what matters is whether the offering has a set time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is a fixed time, not who owns the offering. So when רבי מאיר called offerings 'private' and רבי יעקב called offerings 'communal', they were only arguing about pushing aside שבת. Neither was ruling on whether the כהן גדול's bull is private or communal, so the משנה gives no support to רב עמרם.

keyTerms.meaning: Hold this rule in your hand, meaning 'remember this principle'
Its time is fixed (it has a set date)
A single person, a private owner

steps.whatToRemember: Whether an offering pushes aside שבת and טומאה depends on a fixed time, not on whether it is communal. So the משנה with רבי מאיר and רבי יעקב cannot prove that the כהן גדול's bull is communal.

phrases.english: Rather, hold this rule in your hand:
Anything whose time is fixed
pushes aside Shabbat and ritual impurity
even for an individual;
and anything whose time is not fixed

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דּוֹחֶה לֹא אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא אֶת הַטּוּמְאָה
phrases.english: does not push aside Shabbat or ritual impurity,
even for the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי מאיר (step 12) and רבי יעקב (step 13) both show that 'private' and 'communal' are not the deciding factors, the correct rule is stated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fixed time, not communal ownership, decides whether an offering pushes aside שבת and טומאה.

steps.title: אביי's challenge from a ברייתא about lost offerings
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges (Sefaria: against רבא) with a ברייתא about a lost bull and goat of יום הכפורים. There, רבי (אליעזר) and רבי שמעון explain their ruling with the words 'a חטאת צבור does not die.' This suggests the יום הכפורים bull counts as communal.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged from a ברייתא: If the bull and goat of יום הכפורים were lost and replacements were set aside, all of them are left to die. Likewise, if the goats for עבודה זרה were lost and replacements were set aside, all are left to die. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי (אליעזר) and רבי שמעון say: they graze until they get a blemish. Then they are sold and the money goes to voluntary offerings, because a חטאת צבור is not left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא as an objection. It seems to show that the כהן גדול's bull of יום הכפורים is a communal sin-offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the bull of יום הכפורים among the offerings, and the reason given is 'a חטאת צבור does not die.' That reason only fits if the bull is communal. So the ברייתא seems to settle the question: the bull is a חטאת צבור.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection against him from a תנאי source
He set aside other animals in their place
They graze until they get a blemish

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of bull. The 'פר של יום הכפורים' is the כהן גדול's bull. The 'פר העלם דבר' is a completely different communal bull. The next steps turn on exactly this difference.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:

phrases.aramaic: פַּר וְשָׂעִיר שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁאָבְדוּ,
phrases.english: A bull and goat of Yom Kippur that were lost,
and he set aside others in their place,
all of them are left to die.
And likewise, goats for idolatry that were lost,
and he set aside others in their place,
all of them are left to die. These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi (Eliezer) and Rabbi Shimon say:
phrases.notes: Sefaria reads this name as רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: They graze until they become blemished,
and they are sold, and their money goes to voluntary offerings,
because a communal sin-offering is not left to die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The proof from the משנה was pushed off, so the question was left open. Now אביי brings a new source that seems to call the bull communal.
steps.kashyaTarget: The position that the כהן גדול's bull of יום הכפורים is a private offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא includes the יום הכפורים bull under the reason 'a חטאת צבור does not die,' so the bull must be communal.

steps.title: The bull in the ברייתא is the communal-mistake bull
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the 'bull' in the ברייתא is not the כהן גדול's bull. It is the פר העלם דבר של צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Which bull is meant? The bull for a communal mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The other side answers אביי by reading the word 'bull' in the ברייתא as a different, clearly communal bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bull in the ברייתא is the פר העלם דבר, which everyone agrees is communal, the reason 'a חטאת צבור does not die' fits without saying anything about the כהן גדול's bull. So the bull of יום הכפורים can still be private.

phrases.english: He said to him: What bull is meant?
The bull for a communal mistaken ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers אביי's challenge from Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting which case the source is talking about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'bull' is the כהן גדול's bull of יום הכפורים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's 'bull' is the פר העלם דבר של צבור, so it proves nothing about the כהן גדול's bull.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says 'of יום הכפורים'
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes back: the ברייתא clearly says 'of יום הכפורים,' so it must mean the יום הכפורים bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'of יום הכפורים'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the answer using the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'bull and goat of יום הכפורים.' The פר העלם דבר has nothing to do with יום הכפורים, so the answer seems to clash with the text.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches! (pointing to the wording of the source)

phrases.english: But it teaches 'of Yom Kippur'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the answer given in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא's bull is the פר העלם דבר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'of יום הכפורים' are attached to the bull, which rules out the פר העלם דבר.

steps.title: 'Of יום הכפורים' describes only the goat
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the words 'of יום הכפורים' refer only to the goat, not to the bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it teaches 'of יום הכפורים,' that refers to the goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer reads the ברייתא so that 'of יום הכפורים' describes only the goat. The bull is the separate פר העלם דבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, the ברייתא means 'the bull of a communal mistake, and the goat of יום הכפורים.' Both are communal, so 'a חטאת צבור does not die' fits both. אביי's proof falls away, and the כהן גדול's bull can still be private.

keyTerms.meaning: On the goat, meaning the phrase goes only with the goat

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's ברייתא does not prove that the כהן גדול's bull is communal. Its 'bull' is the פר העלם דבר, and 'of יום הכפורים' describes only the goat.

phrases.english: When it teaches this, it refers to the goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the wording challenge of Step 17 and keeps the answer of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-dividing the words of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Of יום הכפורים' describes both the bull and the goat.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Of יום הכפורים' describes only the goat, so the bull is the פר העלם דבר.

steps.title: A second ברייתא explicitly calls both the bull and the goat 'of יום הכפורים'
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings another ברייתא. It names both the bull and the goat as 'of יום הכפורים' and explains the ruling with 'a חטאת צבור does not die.' This suggests the כהן גדול's bull counts as communal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: If the bull of יום הכפורים and the goat of יום הכפורים were lost, and he set aside others in their place, all of them are left to die. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון say: they graze until they get a blemish, then they are sold and the money goes to voluntary offerings, because a חטאת צבור is not left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks again with a new ברייתא. In this one, the words 'of יום הכפורים' are attached to the bull too, so the last answer cannot work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer said 'of יום הכפורים' described only the goat. Here the phrase is written separately on the bull and on the goat, so the bull must be the כהן גדול's bull. Since the reason given is 'a חטאת צבור does not die,' it seems this bull is a communal offering.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge)
They are left to die (locked away until they die)
They graze until they get a blemish
Voluntary offerings (the money goes toward them)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a repeat of step 15. It is a different ברייתא, and its wording ('פר של יום הכפורים' and 'שעיר של יום הכפורים') blocks the answer from step 18.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא:
The bull of Yom Kippur
and the goat of Yom Kippur
that were lost, and he set aside others in their place —
phrases.notes: Later the originals were found, so there are extra animals.

phrases.english: all of them are left to die; these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi (Eliezer) and Rabbi Shimon say:
They graze until they become blemished
and they are sold, and their money goes to voluntary offerings,
because a communal sin-offering is not left to die.
phrases.notes: This is the phrase אביי is relying on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18's deflection with a ברייתא whose wording cannot be split between bull and goat.
steps.kashyaTarget: The position that the כהן גדול's יום הכפורים bull is not a communal offering, and step 18's reading that 'of יום הכפורים' describes only the goat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא attaches 'of יום הכפורים' to the bull explicitly and gives the reason 'a חטאת צבור does not die.' So the יום הכפורים bull is called communal.

steps.title: Change the wording to 'a sin-offering of partners does not die'
steps.stepSummary: The answer changes the ברייתא's reason. Read it as 'a חטאת השותפין does not die.' The bull is shared by the כהן גדול and his fellow כהנים, but it is not a 'community' offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say 'because a חטאת צבור is not left to die.' Instead, say 'because a חטאת השותפין is not left to die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי by correcting one word in the ברייתא's reason. 'Community' becomes 'partners.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יום הכפורים bull brings atonement for the כהן גדול and all the כהנים, so many people share in it. That is why it is not left to die, like a shared offering. But a group of partners is a different category from a true 'community' (צבור), so the original position stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say... rather say (a wording correction)

phrases.english: Do not say: 'because a communal sin-offering is not left to die,'
rather say: 'because a sin-offering of partners is not left to die.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא שֶׁאֵין חַטַּאת צִבּוּר מֵתָה אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends against step 19 by changing the word the challenge relied on.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation of the ברייתא (changing צבור to שותפין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls the יום הכפורים bull a 'communal' sin-offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bull is a 'partners' sin-offering. Because it is shared, it is not left to die, but it is not formally communal.

steps.title: What difference does 'partners' versus 'community' make?
steps.stepSummary: Either way, the bull is not left to die. So the גמרא asks why the change in wording matters at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what practical difference is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. If the ruling is the same either way, why insist on the word 'partners'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The final ruling in the ברייתא does not change: the extra animal grazes and is not left to die. So the גמרא wants to know where calling it 'partners' instead of 'community' leads to a different law.

phrases.english: And what is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of step 20's correction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the halacha differs depending on whether the כהנים are 'partners' or a 'community.'

steps.title: כהנים do not bring a bull for a mistaken ruling
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up with פר העלם דבר. A true community brings a bull when its court rules wrongly. The כהנים, who are only partners, do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is that the כהנים do not bring a bull for a mistaken ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. It points to a real law that changes depending on whether the כהנים are a 'community.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a court rules wrongly and a community (like a tribe) acts on that ruling, the community brings a פר העלם דבר של צבור. If the כהנים were a 'community,' they would bring this bull too. Since they are only 'partners,' they do not.

keyTerms.meaning: A ruling by the court (here, a mistaken one)
The bull brought for a community's sin based on a mistaken court ruling (פר העלם דבר)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רבא insisted on the word 'partners': the כהנים are not a צבור for the law of פר העלם דבר, even though the יום הכפורים bull is shared and so is not left to die.

phrases.english: That priests do not bring a bull for a mistaken ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the כהנים are partners, not a community, they do not bring a פר העלם דבר when their court rules wrongly.

steps.title: Setting up a proof from a question of רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says 'come and hear' and introduces a question asked by רבי אליעזר. That question will be used as the next proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as רבי אליעזר asked:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is introducing a source that will be quoted next, so the actual proof has not yet appeared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תא שמע' tells us a new source is coming to help settle the open question: whether the כהן גדול's יום הכפורים bull is a private offering or a communal one. The content of רבי אליעזר's question comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as Rabbi (Eliezer) asked:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The partners-versus-community side point of steps 20–22 is closed. The גמרא now brings a new source for the ongoing question of whether the כהן גדול's יום הכפורים bull is private or communal.
steps.raayaObject: The status of the כהן גדול's יום הכפורים bull (private versus communal)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A question of רבי אליעזר (content continues on the next amud)
